memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So that place was called Beersheba, because the two men swore an oath there. After the treaty had been made at Beersheba, Abimelek and Phicol the commander of his forces returned to the land of the Philistines. - Gen 21:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The place gets a name: Beersheba, "the well of the oath" (or "well of seven"). A name is given so that the event will be remembered. Every time someone spoke that name in the years to come, they would recall the peace made there, the covenant sworn, the faithfulness shown. The place became a lasting marker of what God had done.

Throughout Genesis, we've seen this pattern - Abraham building altars, naming wells, marking places where God met him or worked in his life. This is a deeply wise practice. Our memories are short, and we forget quickly. So God's people mark the moments, name the places, build the memorials, so that faithfulness is not forgotten.

We would do well to do the same. When God provides, when He answers prayer, when He brings peace or breakthrough or comfort, it is good to mark it somehow - to write it down, to remember the date, to tell the story. These markers become anchors for our faith in later, harder seasons.

The people of God have always been called to remember. "Remember the wonders he has done" (Ps 105:5). Jesus gave us the bread and cup precisely so we would "do this in remembrance" of Him (Luke 22:19). What "Beershebas" are there in your life - places and moments where God showed His faithfulness? Mark them, remember them, and let them strengthen your trust in the God who is faithful still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What moments of God's faithfulness in your life should you mark and remember?
- How can remembering God's past faithfulness strengthen your faith today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me mark and remember the moments of Your faithfulness. When I forget, bring them back to mind. Let the memory of Your past goodness anchor my faith in every future season. You are faithful still.
Amen.
